cohort: The study included 39 newborn infants diagnosed with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), divided into two groups based on the presence (cardiogenic NEC) or absence (classical NEC) of congenital heart disease (CHD).
finding: Infants with cardiogenic NEC had higher gestational age, birth weight, age at NEC diagnosis, surgical treatment rates, and mortality rates compared to those with classical NEC, indicating that CHD is an important risk factor for a different clinical course of NEC.
mod_finding: There was no difference in mode of delivery between the cardiogenic NEC and classical NEC groups.
